_readme: Real-world dimensions of every vessel and instrument the scene draws. THE ONLY source of object size in the scene.
World unit: 1 world unit = world_unit_mm millimetres. Builders read these via src/scene/dims.js, never a typed size.
Every value is an object with its unit key (mm | ml | deg | count) and EXACTLY ONE provenance key:
src     — a key into `sources` (a standard or a manufacturer/catalogue spec that was actually looked up)
est     — ESTIMATED: no spec was found; the string says what the number is based on. Treat as provisional.
derived — computed from other sourced values in this entry (the expression is given).
`model` names the concrete product the entry describes, so an estimate can be replaced by looking that product up.
Footprint axes: width = scene X (left-right as the camera sees it), depth = scene Z (front-back), height = Y.

clearances._note: Layout rules, not object sizes: gaps the scene keeps between things. Estimated from bench practice.

bench_gap.est: hand-width gap between neighbouring items on a bench

socket_fit.est: radial play between a vessel and the bore/slot that holds it

lift.est: height a carried vessel clears the tallest thing it passes over

contact_epsilon.est: tolerance of the contact check (half a millimetre)
